tweet_summary: Right-leaning account claims a new CBS poll shows Republican approval of Trump 'jumping 3 points to 92.5%' and asks users to amplify; pairs the claim with a clip of Trump greeting Iowa restaurant patrons.
why_note_decision: There is no CBS News poll showing Republican Trump approval at 92.5% (or 92.3%). CBS's published polls in this period (CBS News/YouGov) actually show Trump with a -26 net approval overall; CNN/SSRS at 80% Republican approval, Pew at 68%. The same fabricated 92%+ figure recycles across parody and non-parody accounts. CNN explicitly fact-checked a parallel '100% Republican approval' claim. Reaches >160K views and is presented as breaking news — a note is clearly warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (a) clearly states no such CBS poll exists / CBS has not released a poll with that figure, and (b) gives actual recent Republican-approval numbers from credible polling (e.g. CNN/SSRS ~80%, Pew ~68%, or CBS/YouGov's actual numbers). Strong notes cite CBS News polls archive plus a real outside fact-check (CNN, AP, Reuters) or Pew/Gallup/Quinnipiac numbers. FAIL if the bot just says 'CBS hasn't released this' with only Wikipedia/Rasmussen as supporting links (this is the original note's weakness — raters flagged sources as unreliable). FAIL if the bot declines (the figure is fabricated, high-confidence). FAIL if the bot accepts the 92.5% figure.
reference_note: No CBS News poll shows Republican approval of Trump at 92.5%. The figure does not appear in CBS's poll archive. Recent credible polls of Republicans show much lower numbers — CNN/SSRS ~80% and Pew Research ~68% Republican approval; CBS News/YouGov's own data has Trump's net approval underwater overall. https://www.cbsnews.com/feature/cbs-news-polls/ https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/06/politics/fact-check-trump-approval-rating

original_unhelpful_note.text: CBS has not released a poll showing Republican approval of Trump jumping to 92.5%. No such poll appears on their official polls page, which lists all recent surveys (latest on Iran war, not approval).    https://www.cbsnews.com/feature/cbs-news-polls    Recent approval polls show lower overall ratings:    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_second_Trump_presidency    https://www.rasmussenreports.com/public_content/politics/trump_administration_second_term/trump_approval_index_history_second_term
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substance is correct (no such poll exists), but supporting links lean on Wikipedia and Rasmussen — which raters flagged as missing/unreliable (notHelpfulSourcesMissingOrUnreliable=3). Stronger note would cite CBS's own data, CNN/Pew Republican-approval numbers, and a direct fact-check.

fact_check.notes: No such CBS poll exists. The 92.5% / 92.3% figure recycles across multiple accounts (including parody). CNN/SSRS shows Trump at ~80% among Republicans; Pew at ~68%; CBS/YouGov shows -26 net overall.

importance.lens_rationale: Fabricated approval-rating claims directly degrade public information about political legitimacy and feed manufactured-consensus dynamics; medium reach (~165K views) but pattern is common across many accounts.
